mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive supply signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a disinflationary environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the disinflation signal, or the correlation between CPI decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% each in a month signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and investment in housing bolster economic growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive demand signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST, RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as reduced employment suggests a slowing economy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate below 1% for three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as cheap borrowing costs stimulate investment and economic activity.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of periods with accommodative policy, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
